title: SSO/SAML: IdP compatibility matrix, edge cases, and admin-facing docs for RBAC v2
creator: Priya Desai
description: Summary: Produce an IdP-specific compatibility reference, runbook, and admin-facing documentation for SSO/SAML integrations (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping) targeted at RBAC v2 and audit-logging behaviors. The deliverables are: 1) an IdP compatibility matrix that lists expected SAML attributes, recommended NameID formats, SCIM provisioning caveats, signature/encryption requirements, and known idiosyncrasies; 2) a troubleshooting runbook for operators and customers covering common failures (clock skew, certificate rotation, multiple certs, encrypted assertions, IdP-initiated flows); 3) admin docs for Console that map IdP groups/claims to RBAC v2 roles and explain audit log propagation and retention implications. Goal: reduce onboarding friction, cut Support SSO tickets by 40% for enterprise installs, and ensure RBAC v2 role-mapping is predictable across major IdPs.
acceptance_criteria: A downloadable compatibility matrix (CSV/Markdown) exists and lists attribute names, example values, and required/optional flags for Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping.
Console admin docs include step-by-step mapping examples for group->role, claim-based role binding, and a note on precedence for conflicting claims.

Troubleshooting runbook includes detection steps for signed vs unsigned assertions, common error messages and recovery steps for certificate rollover, and test instructions for IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows.
QA tests: automated integration tests for Okta and Azure AD SAML flows in staging, and a manual test plan for Google Workspace and Ping.
Security review sign-off recorded and a follow-up ticket created for any infra changes needed to support encrypted assertions or alternate signature algorithms.
Links to supporting PRs and Confluence docs are present in the ticket.
Support team playbook snippet added to internal runbook, and at least one customer-facing KB article is drafted.
Docs updated to call out limitations (e.g., SCIM throttling, group-pagination issues) and recommended mitigations.
comments: 2025-01-12 - Priya Desai: Kickoff notes - met with PM to align on scope. Priority is to reduce support churn for Dedicated and Private customers. Identified Okta and Azure as high-volume IdPs; Google Workspace and Ping as high-risk for edge cases.

2025-01-20 - Liam O'Connor: Initial compatibility survey complete. Key differences noted: Azure requires SHA256 signatures by default for apps created in new portals; Okta frequently uses 'email' or 'user.login' as default NameID; Google Workspace sometimes omits group lists unless domain admin consented; Ping returns custom NameID formats and can present multiple certificates.

2025-01-25 - Maya Chen (Security): Raised a requirement to support encrypted assertions for a subset of enterprise customers. Recommended adding a configuration flag in the SAML handler and documenting key rotation steps. Marked for design discussion with runtime team.

2025-01-30 - Liam O'Connor: Draft matrix attached (sso_idp_matrix_v1.csv). Began writing runbook sections for certificate rollover and replay/nonce handling. Created staging test harness for Okta using sample metadata URL.

2025-02-04 - Carlos Rivera (Support): Reported two recurring customer issues: (1) users failing to authenticate after IdP cert rotation because metadata fetch wasn't enabled; (2) role mapping surprises when both group and claim mappings exist. Added examples to acceptance criteria to address these.

2025-02-09 - Priya Desai: Security review requested. Document now includes notes on audit logging: SAML assertion ID should be surfaced in audit logs, SCIM events must map to user lifecycle actions, and admin-level export of SSO audit entries should be available to Enterprise tenants.
2025-02-12 - Liam O'Connor: Updated ticket with PR links and manual test checklist. Beginning documentation handoff to Docs team for copy editing and Console team for UI/UX update estimate.

Action items: finish Google Workspace and Ping manual tests (Liam), add encrypted assertion support design (Maya + runtime), update Console UI to show active SAML certs and last metadata fetch time (Frontend team follow-up ticket).
testing_plan: Automated: add SAML flow smoke tests for Okta and Azure using test metadata and assertion stubs.
Manual: run SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows for Google Workspace and Ping in staging; verify group mappings and NameID variations.
Security: simulate certificate rollover and replay attacks to validate audit logging and alerting.
Docs QA: have Support follow runbook on a mock customer to validate reproducibility.
notes: IdP-specific highlights: Okta - recommend mapping user.email or user.login to NameID and enabling 'Include Credentials in SAML assertion' for group claims; Azure AD - ensure Reply URL and Identifier match Console values exactly and advise customers to use SHA256 for signature algorithm; Google Workspace - ask customers to enable 'Include in SAML' for groups or provision groups via SCIM; Ping - support multiple certs in metadata and document how to select active cert by 'kid' if present. Also log 'assertion_id' and 'saml_response_base64' hash in audit records to aid investigation (PII considerations: do not store raw assertions; store hashes and structured claim extracts).
risks: Customers with strict encrypted-assertion requirements may require runtime changes to support decryption keys; this could slip the release.
SCIM provisioning rate limits and group pagination across IdPs can cause partial syncs and role-mapping drift.
Misconfigured admin mappings could create RBAC elevation risks; require a locking confirmation in Console when mapping groups to admin roles.
Metadata fetching failures during IdP maintenance windows could cause mass-login failures; need fallback behavior or cached metadata warnings in Console.
